evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: H1 'Know what your city council is about to decide, before the meeting.' plus lede 'Commonread reads it, writes each item in plain language, and emails you when your street or a topic you follow is on it' and a neighbourhood+email form with 'Send me alerts for my street'. What, who and next step are all there before scrolling.
evidence.fit: Strongest audience coverage of the pair: a full Spanish section (#espanol) with a yes/no status list, a 'For city clerks and funders: where we are' table, a 'What a summary never does' neutrality block, and 'Open the original agenda item' on every summary. Against the brief: it invents a pilot city ('Linden Falls') and presents its agenda as real, and the no-backend sign-up is routed to alerts@commonread.org, an address the brief never supplied. The 'Send the alert email in Spanish' checkbox promises a capability the brief does not mention.
evidence.distinctiveness: Product-specific ideas: a council-packet excerpt set in Courier caps beside the structured plain-language summary (#how), a yellow highlighter 'mark' motif that is explained ('We highlight the street or topic that matched your alert'), an email-shaped alert preview in the hero. The rest of the structure (three numbered steps, tinted alternating bands, three-column footer) is familiar nonprofit template.
evidence.proof: 1440: the alert card is in the first screen and swaps content per neighbourhood (tested Mill District, Eastgate, Not sure, Downtown). Second screen has the agenda-vs-summary pair. But nothing is labelled as an example: the section says 'Here is one real item from the October 28 agenda', so the proof rests on invented material. Small inconsistency: the Downtown alert cites 'Item 5A' for the $38,000 lighting, while the list and the agenda page put that payment under 5B.
evidence.craft: Serif display type is set well and spacing is consistent. Defects: at 1440 the right column ends at about y=570 while the form runs to 810, leaving an empty block under the alert card; at 768 the nav wraps to a second row with the dark CTA button floating mid-row; at 390 the packet excerpt is dense 13.8px Courier caps; the probe reports one serious axe color-contrast node at 390 and 1440.
evidence.mobile: 390: no menu button, so five nav links wrap into two rows that take about 150px of the first screen. The form stacks well with 48px fields, but the alert-card artifact starts at y=961, below the first screen. After a valid submit the 'Almost there' confirmation starts at y=856, just below the fold. No overflow at 390 or 320.
evidence.honesty: Invented specifics presented as fact with no example label anywhere on the page: 'Here is one real item from the October 28 agenda, next to the summary we sent'; 'Checked against the original by Dana R. (volunteer), Oct 24'; the clerks table says 'Meetings covered: Every regular council meeting since September 2026'; the agenda subpage says 'A copy of the city's posted agenda, kept by Commonread for the pilot.' The fact that sign-up opens your mail client and is handled by hand only appears after you submit. To its credit, the clerks table says 'Partner cities: None yet', 'Funding: None yet' and 'Readers: Too few to quote honestly'.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390. Empty submit marks both fields with red borders and written messages, and moves focus to the select. A bad email ('bad') flags only the email field. The neighbourhood select swaps the alert card with a short fade; there are seven variants, including an empty state for Eastgate ('Nothing about Eastgate...') and a citywide digest. The choice is saved in localStorage. A valid submit fires a prefilled mailto (subject 'Alerts for Downtown', with neighbourhood, email and language in the body) and shows a status message. At 390 and 768 the card update happens offscreen, so you get no visible feedback where you tapped.
evidence.copy: Specific and civic: 'sign up at the chamber door before 6:30 pm', 'Reply "stop" to stop', 'Choose a neighbourhood so we know which items to send.' The Spanish section is natural rather than machine-flat. Button text says what it does. Minor: 'the summary we sent' implies alerts are already being sent.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific promise, a live alert sample and the form are all in view, but the sample carries no example label and the city is invented. 390: headline, lede and form are in view, but no artifact appears before y=961, and the wrapped nav pushes the H1 down to y=190.

problems: Fabricated material presented as real: invented city 'Linden Falls', 'one real item from the October 28 agenda', named volunteers 'Dana R.', 'Luis M.', 'Priya S.', and 'Every regular council meeting since September 2026', with no example label anywhere.
The primary sign-up opens mailto:alerts@commonread.org, an address the brief did not supply, and the manual-email process is only explained after the click.
Phone layout is shrunk rather than recomposed: the nav wraps into two rows with no menu, the alert artifact sits below the first screen, and the confirmation lands below the fold.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The primary action 'Send me alerts for my street' (and the header CTA that anchors to it) submits by setting window.location.href to mailto:alerts@commonread.org?subject=Alerts%20for%20...; the brief supplies no email address. Nothing on the page says before submission that the button opens your email app.

Scroll to 'For city clerks and funders: where we are' and read the 'Meetings covered' row. Search the page for 'sample', 'example' or 'illustrative': there are no matches that label this content.

evidence.clarity: 1440: H1 'Know what the council will decide on your street, before they vote', then a sub that states the mechanism ('a model drafts each summary, a volunteer checks it, and every one links to the original item') and the action ('Pick a neighbourhood and we email you'). The form sits directly below. Slight drift between 'your street' in the headline and the neighbourhood-level alerts.
evidence.fit: Neutrality is shown rather than claimed: the model-draft card strikes 'This would be a welcome boost for a tired block.' with the note 'Struck: an opinion.' Every item has an 'Open item X in the packet' link. The no-backend constraint is reflected in a local 'Not sent yet' status. Weaker on the brief's other audiences: Spanish speakers get one bilingual sentence under the form and a 'Language' definition, and clerks get one paragraph inside #original. Funders get no path at all.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero artifact is the product itself: a digest that pairs official council wording in Termes serif with a plain-language summary in Helvetica, mono item numbers and tag chips, on a paper-and-ink palette with one highlighter yellow. The 'Model draft, as the volunteer saw it' card with del/ins edits is specific to this product. With the logo removed you would still recognise the page.
evidence.proof: 1440: the digest is in the first screen and responds to the neighbourhood select. It is labelled 'Sample agenda' with 'Four items from an illustrative agenda... Not a record of any real council.' Item 6.B is consistent across the digest, the draft stage, the sample alert email and sample-agenda-item.html#item-6b. Each item carries its official text, its summary and a 'Checked by' line.
evidence.craft: Token-driven type and spacing scale, 1px rules, 2px radii, consistent 48px controls. Axe reports nothing at 390 or 1440. Minor: the hero digest runs about 900px below the fold beside a short left column, so the hero ends with a long empty left side; the alert-chip and tags at 13px mono are on the edge of small.
evidence.mobile: 390: a 73x48 'Menu' button opens a 217px vertical list and closes when a link is tapped, but Escape does not close it (aria-expanded stayed true). Form fields are 48px and the button is full width. The digest starts at y=927, below the first screen, so the status sentence updated by the select (y=1118) is offscreen when you choose. The 'Open item ... in the packet' links are about 23px tall. No overflow at 390 or 320.
evidence.honesty: Labels sit next to the material: 'Sample agenda', 'Not a record of any real council', 'Sample alert · illustrative', 'Illustrative text, in the city's own format', a footer disclaimer, and a yellow notice on the sample item page. The weak point is the main action: before you submit, the copy reads 'Always free... Unsubscribe in one click', and 'Not sent yet. Sign-up is not connected to a mailing list...' appears only after the click.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390. The select highlights the matching item's plain-language sentence, shows an 'Alert: Eastside' chip and rewrites the status ('For Riverbend, this agenda would send one alert with item 8.A, and item 11 listed as citywide.'). Westgate gives an explicit no-match message. Both forms validate with written errors ('Choose a neighbourhood first.', 'That email address does not look complete.') and move focus. A valid submit prints a specific 'Not sent yet' message naming the email and area. Gaps: the lower form does not drive the digest; Escape does not close the menu; at 390 the select feedback is offscreen.
evidence.copy: Precise and in the residents' and clerks' own terms: 'second reading', 'consent items are voted on together without discussion', and the checklist 'No opinion words: good, bad, finally, unfortunately, controversial.' Errors and statuses are written, not defaulted. Small lapse: 'Unsubscribe in one click' and 'Always free' read as a live service's boilerplate.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific promise, a labelled and operable sample digest, and the form all sit in one viewport. 390: headline, sub, form and button are in view, but no artifact, and the 'Get alerts for my neighbourhood' label promises a subscription that does not happen yet.

problems: The sign-up's real result ('Not sent yet... not connected to a mailing list') is disclosed only after the click, while the copy before it ('Always free... Unsubscribe in one click') implies a live list.
Spanish-speaking residents and funders get almost nothing: one bilingual sentence and a 'Language' definition for the first, no section at all for the second.

At 390 the digest artifact and its select-driven feedback are below the first screen, so choosing a neighbourhood gives no visible response; Escape does not close the menu; the packet links are about 23px tall.

reason: B builds the page around the product's real job: an operable, clearly labelled sample digest in the first screen and a draft-with-struck-opinions card that proves neutrality, set in a typographic system that reads as civic document rather than startup template. A covers the brief's audiences better (Spanish section, clerks and funders table), but it presents an invented city, agenda and volunteers as real and routes its primary action to an email address the brief never supplied. A would only win if its content were relabelled as a sample and the mailto replaced with an honest local action. Even then, B's artifact is stronger.
